html:
SMTO-POL-0030 — Please answer the permission question that's already waiting

GUID: 76be67d9-403e-5421-a747-4246dbdd490b
Slug: authority-request-pending
Domain: POL · Subsystem: resource-access

What happened

  • SMTO already asked you a permission question that hasn't been answered. It can't ask a different one until you do. The waiting question is unchanged and no new access was given.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Scroll through the conversation to the waiting permission card and choose Authorize this resource for this task or Don't allow. SMTO can only have one open permission question at a time in a task.
  2. Read the card before you choose; it lists exactly what SMTO wants to use and where. A waiting question is not a permission; nothing is allowed until you agree to it.
  3. After you answer, let SMTO continue. If it needs something else, it will show a new card for that. Once the first question is settled, SMTO can ask about the other items on their own.

What success looks like

  • The old card shows your answer, and SMTO either continues or shows a new permission card.

If it still fails

  • If you can't find a waiting card, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same request over and over; that won't clear the waiting question.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • request_resource_access was rejected because a different authority request (of another kind, or not covering every requested resource) is still pending for this task.

What this means

  • The current pending authority request is either for another authority kind or does not cover every requested resource. An identical covered resource request reuses the existing question instead. This rejection leaves the frozen question intact and grants no additional access.

Why this can happen

  • The current pending authority request is either for another authority kind or does not cover every requested resource. An identical covered resource request reuses the existing question instead. This rejection leaves the frozen question intact and grants no additional access.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the active question and the requested resource set; do not replace or expand its frozen choices.

How to fix it

  • Resolve the pending authority request shown in the conversation (allow or deny) before requesting different resources; inspect the run's pending_wait and authority_requests to see which question is active. An identical request already covered by the pending question reuses it instead of failing.
  • Resolve the displayed permission question before requesting different resources.

Retry and execution caution

  • Submit the intended request only after the displayed question has been resolved.

How to verify the fix

  • The active question is resolved and the intended resource request can be evaluated on its own.

What not to do

  • Do not interpret the pending question as permission or submit conflicting approval requests repeatedly.

Technical notes

  • The existing pending question is retained; no access is granted.
  • A pending question says nothing about whether the user will grant access.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
